{{Short description|Characterization of the gamma function}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Wielandt theorem''' [[characterization (mathematics)|characterizes]] the [[gamma function]], defined for all complex numbers <math>z</math> for which <math>\mathrm{Re}\,z > 0</math> by
:<math>\Gamma(z)=\int_0^{+\infty} t^{z-1} \mathrm e^{-t}\,\mathrm dt,</math>
as the only function <math>f</math> defined on the half-plane <math>H := \{ z \in \Complex : \operatorname{Re}\,z > 0\}</math> such that:
* <math>f</math> is [[holomorphic function|holomorphic]] on <math>H</math>;
* <math>f(1)=1</math>;
* <math>f(z+1)=z\,f(z)</math> for all <math>z \in H</math> and
* <math>f</math> is [[bounded function|bounded]] on the strip <math>\{ z \in \Complex : 1 \leq \operatorname{Re}\,z \leq 2\}</math>.
This theorem is named after the mathematician [[Helmut Wielandt]].
